The graph of the function $g(x)$ is shown above. Find the value of $b-a,$ given the following:

- $g(x)\rightarrow -\infty$ as $x\rightarrow a$

- $g(x)\rightarrow \infty$ as $x\rightarrow b$
question.worked_solution:
From the given graph, we see that as $x$ approaches $-1,$ the values of $g(x)$ decrease, approaching $-\infty.$ 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14227291/assets/c5b5723c08edacff5a29e160b225343f565d23bb764a84149ca20ebbe28d4ad3.png)

So, we can write

$$
g(x) \to -\infty \quad \text{as} \quad x \to -1.
$$

Therefore, $a = -1.$

From the given graph, we see that as $x$ approaches $1,$ the values of $g(x)$ increase, approaching $\infty.$ 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14227291/assets/3bf9f0d83f05002952d531fe1dcaa6ad14d7d7c4216a59d9a2d3a4e621b57ef5.png)

So, we can write

$$
g(x) \to \infty \quad \text{as} \quad x \to 1.
$$

Therefore, $b =1.$

Finally,

$$
b - a = 1 - (-1) = 2.
$$
